diagnosis:
This is a PDWF construction for hcp Ti with 18 functions per channel (3d, 4s and 4p on each of the two atoms; 3s and 3p are cut out as an isolated block). The untruncated model is good: eta2 = 4.9 meV. The only failure is the sparse criterion. With every hopping beyond r_c = 8.2 Å removed, eta2 rises to 50 meV. That error comes from the five diffuse functions on each atom. These are s/p/d hybrids with spreads of about 2.0 Å², and their centres sit 0.7–0.9 Å off the Ti sites. They carry nearly all the hopping weight beyond r_c. The four tight d-like functions per atom (0.75–1.0 Å²) carry almost none.

The truncation error falls on the parent bands near E_F and on the bottom s-like band 9 (worst near Γ–A, k_z of about 0.34). So it is a smoothness problem in the subspace, not a fidelity problem inside the frozen window. Both minimisations converged.

The frontier's ladder shows which knob moved the number. With dis_proj_max fixed at 0.99, lowering dis_proj_min from 0.01 to 0.005 cut the truncated eta2 from 131 to 50 meV. Lowering dis_proj_max from 0.99 to 0.95 only took it from 131 to 98 meV. Raising dis_proj_min to 0.02 emptied the projectability window (runs 1–4 were refused). A larger pool of weakly projectable states gives the disentanglement more room to choose a smoother, more localised subspace for the diffuse 4s/4p hybrids. I take the strongest lever, dis_proj_min, one step further. The frontier's own next ladder point (dis_proj_max 0.95) is the weaker lever, so I'm not using it.
